quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Logistics analysts analyse product delivery or supply chain processes to identify or recommend changes, and may manage route activity such as invoicing and shipment tracing.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Logistics Analysts) include Supply Chain Analyst, Logistics Analyst, Material Supply Planner and Transportation Analyst.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.

sections.heading: What a supply chain analyst does
paragraphs: Logistics analysts analyse product delivery or supply chain processes to identify or recommend changes, and may manage route activity such as invoicing and shipment tracing.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Logistics Analysts. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Track the flow of products from origin to final delivery.
Keep logistics databases accurate and up to date.
Interpret data on availability, reliability and other supply chain measures.
Recommend improvements to existing or planned logistics processes.
